What are your hopes for the Godzilla (2014) Sequel?

I am more excited to see what Toho (re)does with the character than Legendary at this point. I found Godzilla 2014 to be really disappointing overall, but too over-hyped by fans. I really have no desire to see an American take on any of the classic monsters since I'm positive they will make drastic changes to them for the sake of "realism."
I understand it let down a lot of people. What did you personally find wrong with it? Also, get on the Japan-Godzilla hype train because Hideaki Anno of Evangelion fame is directing it.

1. Godzilla was not the focus of the picture, the MUTOs were. The movie feels like a sequel for this reason, yet the only exposition we get on Godzilla is literally a slide slow presentation.

  2. Godzilla's design is not that interesting, and the things that I dislike about it are greater than the things I actually like. Giving Godzilla webbed hands and gills for the sake of realism is stupid. It was totally unnecessary to make his design more realistic not only because he's a giant fucking dinosaur which is physically impossible, but due to the subtext that somehow 60 years of design had some sort of 'realism' deficit that the American's finally fixed. So was giving him comically undersized feet.

  3. In the Japanese series, Godzilla was created by nuclear weapons. The first film ends with Dr. Yamane saying, "if we continue to test nuclear weapons, another Godzilla will appear." In the 2014 film, the American's nuclear program is an attempt to KILL Godzilla after they accidentally wake him up with a submarine (nuclear other otherwise, the symbolism is gone). Couple that with the MUTOs personifying the nuclear threat in this movie, this Godzilla had absolutely no subtext outside of "a force to balance nature" which roughly translates to "Godzilla needs to kill the bad guys by the end of the picture."

  4. The film, despite being beautifully shot with some great effects sequences was incredibly stupid and full of plot holes. Edwards went for the emotion of a sequence rather than logic. For example, man sized MUTO cacoons leaving giant craters outside of the Yucca Mountain nuclear waste dump (which is NOT within binocular distance of Las Vegas) but also the Philippine Jungle at the start of the movie.

  5. The marketing of the movie flat out lied to the audience by marketing the film as a dark movie about the dangers of Godzilla and then swapping in the MUTOs for those sequences while leaving Godzilla a super hero.

  6. Godzilla was a super hero. Any of the deaths that are implied (because they don't show him causing on-screen death) are and were purely accidentally. He never goes on a rampage, every instance of him destroying or killing someone was purely a result of him trying to get at the actual bad guys of the movie.

  7. Godzilla was a pussy in this movie. He got his ass kicked by monsters that essentially only used physical attacks. His nuclear breath was pitiful compared to even average levels of power you see in most Japanese films.

  8. Godzilla was not in the picture enough. I mean this by run time it is one of the least, and due to the fact it takes nearly an hour to show him on screen outside of the opening credit sequence.

  9. Despite this being billed as a giant monster movie, this film actually focused on one of the worst family drama stories I have seen in a long time. Gareth Edwards cannot direct human actors, yet he feels inclined to shove their blandless and garbage acting down the audience throats. He pursues this vision to the point where he cuts away from actual interesting parts of the movie to show characters which in in peril, who I'd rather prefer died.

I am over the moon with the job Edwards and Legendary did. It's a very by-the-book Showa-style Godzilla film, with a super slow buildup, and a big monster fight payoff at the end. Not unlike Three Headed Monster, Monster Zero, or Godzilla vs The Thing.

I have all the confidence Edwards knows what he's doing and will knock it out of the park once again. First thing I'm looking forward to is his Star Wars movie though, which sounds great to me!

What do I expect? More of the same. In the end it's all about the monsters, Godzilla 2014 did a good job making sure that's what it was really all about when it was said and done. Sure those pesky humans have to come along for the ride, but whatever. Can't wait!
It is all about the monsters! Though it's confirmed we're going to see the old monsters in this one, would you rather have new ones or the old ones?
